newsitem.title: UK: LME routine up to mid-session, copper dips.
newsitem.headline: LME routine up to mid-session, copper dips.

text.p: Trading in base metals remained slow and routine up to the morning recess, traders said on Wednesday, adding that the LME option declaration passed smoothly and had little impact.
Flagship copper settled between July strikes, though late morning speculative selling knocked three months delivery to $2,383, a $10 loss.
Traders said the selling followed another LME stocks rise and the market's inability to break above $2,400 in early trading.
Despite the fall the nearby spreads remained tight. Cash to three months backwardation was last indicated at $125/$130 after earlier dipping to $120/$125.
Traders said the tight nearbys should offer support, though downtrending charts may see an attack on $2,375 support in later trading.
A breach of this level could see a fall to $2,350.
Elsewhere, zinc held near to 6-3/4 year highs amid falling stocks and physical demand. Prices earlier hit $1,455 on fund buying only to be capped by trade selling. It was last at $1,449, up $12/
Aluminium was attempting to build a base above $1,600, though the fall in copper saw prices retreat from resistance around $1,615 to $1,607, a $4 gain.
Nickel was quiet and last at $6,860, down $70. Traders said a stocks rise helped to dent sentiment. They beleived that Russian material was delivered into LME Gothenburg warehouses.
Tin dipped $10 to $5,520 after earlier tradebuying dried up.
Lead was last at $630, down $6, while alloy was $1,455/65, against $1,450/$55.
